sections.h2: Rice straw alone could make 17.4 Mt of the 56.6 Mt of eligible char

chart.title: Rice straw, cotton stalk and wheat straw lead the eligible char
chart.sub: Eligible char by residue, Mt a year; bagasse counted at half weight.

sections.means: Rice straw is the largest single feedstock, and the model counts bagasse at half because mills already burn it.
sections.todo: Start with the residues that are both large and genuinely spare, rather than counting every tonne of surplus.

sections.h2: Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana hold the least soil carbon

chart.title: The lowest carbon soils are in long-farmed plains and dry lands
chart.sub: Organic carbon index, 1 = all samples low, 3 = all high.
chart.source: Soil Health Card index, MoSPI EnviStats 2024.

sections.means: Soil carbon reflects decades of climate and practice, so a decade of harvest growth barely shows in it.
sections.todo: Aim biochar at the depleted plains rather than at the states whose harvests grew fastest.

sections.means: Policy money in Punjab and Haryana goes to machines and non-burning bonuses, not to char.
